video.title: The Ruthless Daughter Of Jezebel: She Killed Her Own Family
video.description:
Athaliah was the daughter of Jezebel and one of the most wicked queens in the Bible. After her son died, she took the throne and tried to destroy the entire royal family. But one child survived.

This video tells the full story of Athaliah—her rise to power, her cruel reign, and her shocking downfall.

#Athaliah #BibleStory #BibleHistory #OldTestament #Christianity

transcript.text: There was a woman in the Bible whose name has been remembered for generations as one of the most evil queens in the Bible.
She was ruthless, obsessed with power, and she wanted the throne so badly that she was willing to kill her own family just to take it.
She became known as the mistress of evil.
For generations, her name has been remembered as one of the darkest names in the history of Judah.
Her story is filled with power, betrayal, violence, and a hunger for the throne that would push her to do the unthinkable.
But how did she become this wicked, and what made her willing to go this far?
This is the story of Athaliah.
Before we get into the story, make sure you hit subscribe, like the video, and share it with someone who might enjoy this.
Athaliah was born into a royal family where power was everything.
Her father was King Ahab and her mother was Jezebel.
She grew up watching her family rule Israel and watching her mother use her position to get what she wanted.
Jezebel was ruthless.
She supported the worship of Baal, helped bring Baal worship into Israel, and had prophets of the Lord hunted down and killed.
Athaliah grew up surrounded by that kind of power.
She saw what happened when a royal family refused to give up control.
Eventually, Athaliah married Jehoram.
He was the son of Jehoshaphat, who was the king of Judah.
This wasn't just a normal marriage, it was a political marriage meant to bring the two royal families closer together.
Now, at this point, Israel had already been divided into two kingdoms.
There was Israel in the north where Athaliah's family came from, and there was Judah in the south where Jehoram's family ruled.
So Athaliah's marriage to Jehoram connected these two powerful families.
Jehoshaphat had several sons.
Jehoram was his firstborn, so he was the one who would become king.
Before Jehoshaphat died, he gave his other sons silver, gold, valuable gifts, and fortified cities.
After his death, Jehoram became king of Judah.
Athaliah was now beside him as queen.
And during Jehoram's rule, Judah began moving further and further away from God.
Then he did something horrifying.
After becoming king, he had his own brothers killed so no one could stand in his way or threaten his throne.
Athaliah was right there beside him during this period and her influence over the royal family continued to grow.
Things started going badly for him.
The Philistines and some Arabs attacked Judah.
They came into the country, raided the royal palace and took the king's possessions.
They also took his wives and some of his sons.
Yes, Jehoram had more than one wife.
One of his sons, Ahaziah, was not taken in the attack.
Later, the prophet Elijah sent him a letter.
Elijah warned him that because of his wickedness, God would bring judgment on him and his family.
Not long after that, Jehoram became terribly sick.
He developed a horrible disease in his intestines.
He suffered with it for about two years.
It became so bad that his intestines eventually came out because of the disease.
After ruling for eight years, Jehoram died from his illness.
His son Ahaziah became king.
Ahaziah was young and his mother Athaliah still had a strong influence over him.
The Bible says that she encouraged him to do evil.
He also did what was wrong in God's eyes and continued the same idol worship they had brought into the royal family.
But unfortunately, he didn't stay king for long.
Ahaziah went to visit Joram.
Joram was Athaliah's brother and he was now the king of Israel.
At that time, a man named Jehu had been sent to wipe out Athaliah's family in Israel.
Jehu killed Joram, and when Ahaziah tried to escape, Jehu's men caught up with him and killed him too.
Ahaziah had been king for only about a year.
Now Athaliah had lost her son, and Judah had been left without its king.
Listen, Ahaziah had children of his own, meaning one of them could eventually become king.
Athaliah wanted the throne for herself.
So as soon as she saw that the throne was empty, she made a horrible decision.
She decided to get rid of anyone who could possibly take it from her.
The Bible says Athaliah set out to destroy all the royal offspring.
That meant the children in her own family were now in danger.
These were her own grandchildren, and Athaliah wanted all of them dead.
While the royal children were being killed, one child was secretly taken away before they could reach him.
His name was Joash.
Joash was the son of Ahaziah, which made him Athaliah's grandson.

transcript.text: Then he divided the guards and placed them around the temple.
They were there because Joash was still in danger.
If Athaliah's soldiers got to him, they could kill him before the people could recognize him as king.
So the guard surrounded Joash with weapons in their hands.
Their job was to protect the boy.
Anyone who tried to break through and reach him was to be killed.
Everything was now ready.
Joash was brought out in front of the people.
He was only seven years old, but he was the surviving heir of the royal family.
Jehoiada placed the crown on his head and declared him king.
Then the people began celebrating.
Trumpets were blown.
The people shouted, long live the king.
The sound could be heard throughout the area.
Judah had its rightful king again.
But Athaliah was still in the palace.
She heard the noise.
She didn't know what was happening, so she went to the temple to find out.
When she arrived, she saw the people celebrating.
Then she looked toward the crowd and there he was, a little boy standing there with a crown on his head.
Athaliah knew exactly who he was, Joash, her grandson, the child she thought had been killed with the rest of the royal family.
He was alive and he was standing in front of the people as king.
Athaliah tore her clothes and shouted, Treason, treason.
But by then the people had had enough.
They were no longer standing behind Athaliah.
Jehoiada ordered the guards to take her away.
They didn't kill her inside the temple because it was considered a sacred place.
They took Athaliah to the horse gate at the palace and that is where she was killed.
Her six-year rule was over.
The woman who had taken the throne by destroying her own family's future was no longer queen.
Joash was now king.
She had spent years supporting the worship of Baal and that influence had spread through Judah.
So after she was killed, they went to the temple of Baal.
They tore it down.
They destroyed its altars and idols.
They also killed Mattan, the priest of Baal.
The people then renewed their commitment to the Lord.
After that, they took Joash to the royal palace.
He sat on the throne of Judah, and remember, this boy was only seven years old.
He had spent almost his entire life hidden away from the woman who wanted him dead.
Now he was sitting on the throne she had taken for herself.
Jehoiada became an important guide to Joash during his early years as king.
And while Jehoiada was alive, Joash did what was right in the eyes of the Lord.
Later, Joash had the temple of the Lord restored after years of neglect during Athaliah's rule.
And yeah, they all lived happily ever after.
But seriously, there's a lesson here.
You can't build your life on wickedness and expect everything to work out in the end.
You might get what you want for a while.
You might get the money, the position, the attention, or the power you've been chasing.
And for a moment it might look like you've won.
But none of that is worth losing yourself over.
Don't let pride, greed, jealousy, or the need to be in control change the kind of person you become.
